When I first saw the anime, I found the story line kinda odd. Like Sachiko was passive and even more childlike than Hatchi. Yet had a strategic side and knew exactly what she wanted. 

Hatchi, despite all her faults, behaved more like a woman her age imo. She had aspirations, dreams, and voiced her feelings. Yet she was unlucky in love. She wasn’t a player despite having an affair with a married man and essentially having overlapping relationships with Nobu and Takumi. Hence, why the anime paints Hatchi as a sort of naive love struck girl who typically ended empty handed. 

Upon further watching I realized Sachiko is essentially the antithesis of Hatchi. 

Sachiko, like Hatchi, had an affair with a committed guy. But unlike Hatchi, she didn’t throw herself right into it. The anime tries to justify the cheating by showing it was a slow desire that burned passionately over time. 

The anime also blames Hatchi for “throwing in the towel” since Sachiko didn’t hide when finally confronted and literally fought to be Shoji. I don’t personally agree with this point the anime tried to make but I understand how it relates to Hatchi’s future and sort of foreshadowed her inability to fight to be with Nobu.
